text: Sometimes two tables need to connect more than one way. Here's how Power BI decides which connection actually counts by default.

ProjectTickets has both an OpenedBy column and a SubmittedBy column — both could reasonably relate to EmployeeRole. Two valid relationships, same two tables. Power BI can only treat one as the default: active.
If the wrong one ends up active, your report isn't broken — it's just answering a different question than you meant.
Here, OpenedBy is active, so this visual only shows project sponsors — the people who open tickets — instead of everyone who actually submitted one.
Fix it in Manage relationships: uncheck OpenedBy, check SubmittedBy. Only one can be active between the same two tables, so checking one automatically unchecks the other.

An inactive relationship isn't gone — a DAX measure can activate it on demand with USERELATIONSHIP, which you'll use later in the course. Next, final lesson of the chapter: putting all of this together into one complete model.
